title: Diagnosing Vertigo and Dizziness
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_vestibular
summary: Kuliah tentang pendekatan diagnosis vertigo dan pusing yang mencakup klasifikasi berbasis gejala (vertigo, presinkop, disekuilibrium, pusing non-spesifik), diferensiasi perifer vs sentral, fitur anamnesis kunci, manuver Dix-Hallpike untuk BPPV, pemeriksaan HINTS untuk sindrom vestibular akut, serta gangguan vestibular umum termasuk BPPV, penyakit Meniere, neuritis vestibular, dan migrain vestibular. Menekankan perbedaan kritis antara penyebab sentral yang berbahaya dan penyebab perifer yang jinak.
Four types of dizziness: vertigo (spinning), presyncope (lightheadedness), disequilibrium (imbalance), nonspecific dizziness
TIMING is key: seconds = BPPV; minutes-hours = Meniere/TIA; hours-days = vestibular neuritis/migraine; continuous = central
HINTS examination (Head Impulse, Nystagmus, Test of Skew) is more sensitive than MRI for stroke in acute vestibular syndrome
learning_goals: Mengklasifikasikan pusing ke dalam empat kategori gejala
Membedakan vertigo perifer dari sentral menggunakan fitur klinis
Melakukan manuver Dix-Hallpike untuk diagnosis BPPV
Menerapkan pemeriksaan HINTS untuk sindrom vestibular akut
Mengenali red flags yang memerlukan neuroimaging gawat

Any acute vestibular syndrome with neurological signs or vascular risk factors should be treated as stroke until proven otherwise

sections.title: Klasifikasi Pusing

content.text: Dizziness is classified into four symptom categories to guide the diagnostic approach. VERTIGO: Illusion of movement (spinning, tilting, swaying); indicates vestibular system dysfunction. PRESYNCOPE: Lightheadedness, feeling faint; suggests cardiovascular or systemic cause (orthostatic hypotension, arrhythmia, anemia). DISEQUILIBRIUM: Unsteadiness, imbalance; suggests proprioceptive, visual, cerebellar, or motor deficits. NONSPECIFIC DIZZINESS: Vague head sensation; may indicate psychiatric (anxiety, hyperventilation), metabolic, or medication causes.
Vertigo: ilusi gerakan (putar, miring, goyang)
Presinkop: pusing gelap, mau pingsan
Disekuilibrium: tidak stabil, kehilangan keseimbangan
Non-spesifik: sensasi kepala tidak jelas

sections.title: Vertigo Perifer vs Sentral

content.text: Differentiating peripheral from central vertigo is critical for patient safety. PERIPHERAL VERTIGO: More intense spinning, severe nausea/vomiting, horizontal-rotatory nystagmus with fast phase away from affected ear, fatigable nystagmus, symptoms provoked/worsened by position changes, no neurological deficits, hearing loss may be present (Meniere), direction-fixed nystagmus. CENTRAL VERTIGO: Less intense spinning, mild nausea, vertical/pure vertical nystagmus, non-fatigable, may occur in any position, neurological deficits common (diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, weakness, ataxia), no hearing loss, direction-changing nystagmus, severe gait instability.
Vertical nystagmus = central cause until proven otherwise - requires urgent MRI

sections.title: Gangguan Vestibular Umum

content.text: BPPV (BENIGN PAROXYSMAL POSITIONAL VERTIGO): Brief episodes (<1 minute) of intense spinning triggered by specific head positions; caused by otoconia displacement in posterior semicircular canal; diagnosed with Dix-Hallpike maneuver; treated with Epley canalith repositioning maneuver. MENIERE DISEASE: Episodes lasting 20 minutes to 12 hours, with fluctuating hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness; endolymphatic hydrops; dietary salt restriction, diuretics. VESTIBULAR NEURITIS: Sudden onset severe vertigo lasting days, post-viral, no hearing loss; positive head impulse test toward affected side; treated with steroids, antiemetics, vestibular rehabilitation. VESTIBULAR MIGRAINE: Vertigo episodes 5 minutes to 72 hours, migraine history, photophobia/phonophobia during vertigo; treated with migraine prophylaxis.

sections.title: HINTS Examination

content.text: HINTS examination is a three-component bedside test for acute vestibular syndrome (AVS: acute onset continuous vertigo with nystagmus, nausea, imbalance lasting >24 hours). It is MORE SENSITIVE than MRI for detecting stroke in the first 24-48 hours. H - HEAD IMPULSE TEST: Rapid head turn while patient fixates on examiner's nose. Normal (corrective saccade) = peripheral lesion = reassuring. Abnormal (no corrective saccade) = central lesion = dangerous. I - NYSTAGMUS: Direction-changing nystagmus on gaze = central. Direction-fixed = more likely peripheral. Vertical nystagmus = central. N - TEST OF SKEW: Alternate cover test looking for vertical correction movement. Skew deviation present = central lesion. INTERPRETATION: Any one abnormal component = central cause = urgent MRI. All three normal = peripheral cause. HINTS PLUS: Add hearing test (fingers rub); acute hearing loss with AVS suggests AICA stroke (central).
H: Head impulse - normal (saccade korektif) = perifer; abnormal = sentral
I: Nistagmus - direction-changing = sentral; vertikal = sentral
N: Test of skew - skew deviation = sentral
Salah satu abnormal = sentral (stroke), MRI segera
HINTS PLUS: tambah tes pendengaran (AICA stroke)
HINTS is MORE sensitive than MRI for stroke in the first 24-48 hours of AVS

sections.title: Algoritma Diagnostik

content.text: DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH: Step 1 - Classify symptom type (vertigo vs presyncope vs disequilibrium vs nonspecific). Step 2 - If vertigo: determine timing (seconds/minutes/hours/days/continuous). Step 3 - Apply HINTS if AVS present. Step 4 - Perform Dix-Hallpike if brief positional vertigo. Step 5 - Look for red flags: new headache, neurological deficits, severe gait instability, vertical nystagmus, direction-changing nystagmus, vascular risk factors. RED FLAGS requiring urgent imaging: any central signs on HINTS, associated neurological deficits, severe continuous vertigo in high-risk vascular patient, head trauma, new severe headache.
Klasifikasi tipe pusing
Tentukan timing (detik/menit/jam/hari/kontinu)
HINTS untuk AVS
Dix-Hallpike untuk vertigo posisi singkat
Cari red flags
